correctness.rationale: The boundary map B(x)=(x_1,x_1+x_2,...,x_{n-1}+x_n,x_n) identifies the spatial Boolean cube with even words of length m=n+1 and sends the interval [a,b] to the weight-two generator at coordinates a-1,b, indexed from zero. Its dual gives the frozen prefix signs. The unnormalized eigenvalue is ((m-2j)^2-m)/2, with binom(n,j) frequency representatives having first coordinate zero and weight j. It vanishes only for m=s^2, when the two represented layers give total nullity binom(s^2,s(s-1)/2) by reflection and Pascal. The maximum absolute eigenvalue is the degree n(n+1)/2. At resonance, the nearest allowed absolute coordinate levels off s are s-2 and (if available) s+2, giving smallest nonzero absolute eigenvalue 2(s-1), including s=2. The condition number is on the surviving subspace, not the full singular operator. The complement of the zero-frequency mask has inverse Walsh kernel with the two stated Krawtchouk terms. Its counting-measure endpoint norms equal the absolute row/column sum. Averaging conjugates of any projection over translations fixes the range pointwise and does not increase either norm; Fourier diagonalization makes the averaged projection unique. Off resonance the projection is the identity. Stirling applied at the offset s/2 from m/2 (one standard deviation for a fair binomial of size m=s^2) gives the stated 2 sqrt(2/(pi e))/s lost fraction along resonances.

evidence: Setting K_2=0 is just (m-2j)^2=m; representatives at zero have weight j_- or its complement, and the smaller layer alone indexes all zero characters of the even subgroup. Their unnormalized sum on an even word v is exactly K_{j_-}(|v|;m), by grouping all weight-j_- subsets by intersection with supp(v). Therefore the range projector is delta_0(v)-K_{j_-}(|v|;m)/2^{m-1}. Summing absolute values over even Hamming shells is the claimed endpoint expression in equivalent coordinates. The matrix row/column sum and group averaging determine the sharp projection norm without optimizing over other operators.
